sentences.text: The applicant Khuman S/o Veer Singh Bhura Patliya (who is lodged in jail since 11.02.2021) in Miscellaneous Criminal Case No.3778/2023 has filed THIRD application; and his earlier FIRST bail application (MCRC No.19713/2021) has already been dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 17.06.2021; and thereafter his SECOND bail application (MCRC No.31291/2021) has already been dismissed by this Court as withdrawn vide order dated 05.05.2022.

The applicant Madhulal S/o Kanhaji Parmar (who is lodged in jail since 11.01.2022) in Miscellaneous Criminal Case No.5429/2023 has filed SECOND application; and his earlier FIRST bail application (MCRC No.24025/2022) has already been dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 28.11.2021.

The applicant Mukesh Neema S/o Late Shankrala (who is lodged in jail since 03.01.2019) in Miscellaneous Criminal Case No.6173/2023 has filed THIRD application; and his earlier two MCRC Nos.3778, 5429 & 6173 of 2023 bail applications have already been dismissed by this Court as withdrawn and having rendered infructuous vide order dated 22.04.2021 and 17.06.2021, whereas his application (MCRC No.31315/2021) for temporary bail on the ground of his ailment was allowed for a period of three months vide order dated 16.08.2021.
Miscellaneous Criminal Case No.3778/2023
Miscellaneous Criminal Case No.5429/2023

The allegations against applicant Khuman S/o Veer Singh Bura Patliya, Madhulal and other accused persons are that of defalcation of Government money to the tune of Rs.5,04,34,139/- (rupees five crore four lakh thirty four thousand one hundred thirty nine only) in Development Block Udaipur,
District Alirajpur (MP), as it is alleged that when the Officers of the Accountant General, Madhya Pradesh, Gwalior inspected the accounts of the said Development Block for a period from 2016 to 2018, it was found that large scale of financial irregularities have been committed by the various officers including the present applicant (s).
Various details of the financial irregularities committed by the applicants have also been narrated in detail in the Final report/Charge sheet.
Shri Vivek Singh, learned counsel appearing for the applic- ant Khuman Singh has submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the case.
He is a retired person and the final MCRC Nos.3778, 5429 & 6173 of 2023 conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficiently long time
and as the prosecution has cited as many as 67 (sixty seven) prosecu- tion witnesses and until now, only one witness has been ex- amined in the trial Court
. The matter relates to documentary evidence only.

The allegation against the applicant (Madhulal S/o Kanhaji Parmar) is that he was serving as a Block Education Officer, Uda- igarh, Tehsil Jobat, District Alirajpur from 14.09.2016 to 03.01.2017 and against him also, similar allegations have been levelled of defalcation of various amounts and the allegation against him is that the applicant misappropriated a sum of Rs.42,00,000/- (rupees forty two lakhs).
Miscellaneous Criminal Case No.6173/2023

In this case, the allegation against the applicant (Mukesh Neema S/o Late Shankrala) is that of his involvement in the aforesaid case wherein a total defalcation amount Rs.5,04,34,139/- (rupees five crore four lakh thirty four thousand one hundred Mukesh Neema vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121604932/
3 thirty nine only).

sentences.text: Heard.

On due consideration of the rival submissions and perusal of the case diary as also looking to the seriousness of the offence, this Court is not inclined to allow the present applica- tions MCRC No.3778/2023 and MCRC No.5429/2023 (Khuman and Madhulal Parmar), as there is no change in the circumstances MCRC Nos.3778, 5429 & 6173 of 2023 also; and the applicants have not come up with any new ground for their release on bail.

However, considering the fact that applicant Mukesh Neema is lodged in jail since 03.01.2019 and has completed more than four years in jail, and only one prosecution witness has been examined until now, his application deserves to be al- lowed, as the prosecution has cited as many as 67 (sixty seven) prosecution witnesses and it is apparent that the final conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficiently long time.

On due consideration of rival submissions and perusal of the case diary including the document (s)
filed on record

, this Court finds force with the contentions raised by Shri Digpal Singh Rathore,
learned counsel for the applicant in Miscellaneous Criminal Case No.6173/2023.
Accordingly, without commenting anything on merits of the matter, the present application for grant of bail is allowed.

The applicant (Mukesh Neema S/o Late Shankrala) is directed to be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only)
with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court for his / her appearance, as and when directed.
The applicant shall be abide by the conditions as enumerated under Section 437 (3) of Cr.P.C.

This order shall be effective till the end of the trial, MCRC Nos.3778, 5429 & 6173 of 2023 however,
in case of bail jump, it shall become ineffective.

AND, so far as other two applicants (Khuman S/o Veer Singh Bura Patliya and Madhulal S/o Kanhaji Parmar) are concerned, no case for grant of bail is made out, at this stage; however, they can renew their prayer after completion of Three years of incarceration, or after material witnesses are examined in the trial court, whichever is earlier, considering the fact that in case of co-accused (Mukesh Neema S/o Late Shankrala), whose bail application has been allowed by this very order looking to the period of incarceration.
Accordingly, Miscellaneous Criminal Case No.6173/2023 is hereby allowed; and Miscellaneous Criminal Case No.3778/2023, Miscellaneous Criminal Case No.5429/2023 stand dismissed.
Certified copy as per rules.
